examples.en: After standing and working all day, I'm going to wreck my body.

examples.ko: 젊을 때 무리하면 나이 들어 골병들어요.
examples.en: If you overwork when you are young, your body breaks down when you get old.

examples.ko: 아버지는 오랫동안 힘든 일을 하다가 골병드셨어요.
examples.en: My father did hard work for a long time and ended up with chronic ailments.
I nearly ruined my body carrying the moving boxes alone.

examples.ko: 야근이 계속되면 몸이 골병들 수 있어요.
examples.en: If overtime goes on, your body can get seriously worn down.
If you don't rest early, you'll break down, so be careful.

explain: 겉으로는 잘 안 보이지만 오랫동안 쌓인 피로나 무리 때문에 몸속이 상하는 것을 말해요. '골병이 들다'로도 쓰고, 주로 몸이 상한 것에 써요. 어간이 'ㄹ'로 끝나서 '골병드니까', '골병드셨어요'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요.

phrases.example: 무거운 짐을 매일 들면 허리에 골병이 들어요.
phrases.en: If you carry heavy loads every day, your back gets worn out for good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골병들다'를 조사와 함께 풀어 쓴 꼴이고 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the spaced-out form of 골병들다 with a particle and means the same.

phrases.en: Take breaks while you work so you don't wear out your body.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 조언할 때 쓰는 연결 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting phrase used when advising someone to be careful.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to ruin your health

phrases.en: If you overdo it, your body gets damaged.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler and broader expression than 골병들다.
phrases.en_equiv: for one's body to be damaged

explain_en: It means your body is damaged inside from long-built-up fatigue or overwork, even if it doesn't show outside. It is also said as '골병이 들다' and is mostly used for physical damage. The stem ends in 'ㄹ', so the ㄹ drops: '골병드니까', '골병드셨어요'.

examples.en: The doctor picked up the scalpel and began the surgery.
A scalpel is very sharp, so you have to be careful.
The scalpels are laid out cleanly in the operating room.
The nurse handed the doctor a scalpel.
The students dissected a frog with a scalpel.
With just one scalpel, he finished a hard operation.

explain: 수술할 때 쓰는 작은 칼이에요. 일상에서는 '수술용 칼'이라고도 해요. '메스를 가하다'는 문제를 고치려고 과감하게 손댄다는 비유로도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: We have to take a scalpel to the outdated system.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 고치려고 과감하게 손댄다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Figurative: to take bold action to fix a problem.

explain_en: A small knife used in surgery, also called 수술용 칼. The phrase 메스를 가하다 is used figuratively for taking bold action to fix a problem.

examples.en: The doctor stitched up the deep wound right away.

examples.ko: 다친 부위를 봉합한 뒤에 주사를 맞았어요.
examples.en: After the injured area was stitched, I got a shot.

examples.ko: 정부가 갈등을 봉합하려고 계속 노력하고 있어요.
examples.en: The government keeps trying to patch up the conflict.
Even after the wound is stitched, you have to be careful for a few days.

examples.ko: 싸움을 대충 봉합했지만 마음은 풀리지 않았어요.
examples.en: We patched up the fight roughly, but our feelings were not settled.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 갈등을 봉합하고 다시 손을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The two companies settled their conflict and joined hands again.

explain: 목적어로 '상처'나 '갈등'이 자주 와요. 갈등을 봉합한다고 하면 뿌리부터 풀었다기보다 일단 수습했다는 느낌이에요. 일상에서 옷이나 천은 '꿰매다'라고 말해요.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 오해를 풀고 갈등을 봉합했어요.
phrases.en: The two cleared up the misunderstanding and patched up their conflict.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use: getting a conflict under control for now.

phrases.en: The wound is deep, so it needs to be stitched right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사가 꼭 해야 할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something a doctor must do.

phrases.en: I sewed up the torn pants with a needle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 천에는 '봉합하다' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this instead of 봉합하다 for clothes and fabric.

explain_en: Its object is often '상처' (wound) or '갈등' (conflict). Saying you 봉합 a conflict suggests it was settled for now rather than solved at the root. For clothes or cloth in daily life, say '꿰매다'.

en: to perform a medical procedure; to perform surgery

examples.en: The doctor performed the procedure personally.
This clinic does the treatment with lasers.
It takes about thirty minutes to do the procedure.
How will you treat this area?
The spot treated yesterday still hurts.
It is safer when a specialist does the procedure.

explain: '시술하다'는 치료하는 사람이 주어예요. 받는 사람은 '시술을 받다'라고 해요. 큰 치료는 '수술하다', 가볍게 몸에 하는 치료는 '시술하다'를 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: The director performs the procedure personally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람을 높이는 말이에요. 병원에서 직원이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Honors the person receiving it. Hospital staff often use it.

phrases.en: It didn't hurt during the procedure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료가 진행되는 시간을 말할 때 써요. '-는 동안'을 붙이면 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time while the treatment is going on. Just add -는 동안.

phrases.en: We don't perform a procedure for small wounds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료를 하지 않는다는 부정형이에요. 의사가 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning no procedure is done. Used when a doctor explains.

explain_en: The subject of 시술하다 is the person giving the treatment; the patient says '시술을 받다' instead. For major operations Koreans say 수술하다, and for lighter treatments on the body they often use 시술하다.

examples.en: I press my shoulders firmly with my fingers.
My neck was stiff, so I pressed on it myself.
Mom pressed on my back for me.
They say pressing on this spot is good for digestion.
I learned how to press on the soles of the feet.
Please don't press too hard.

explain: 몸의 한 곳을 손가락이나 손바닥으로 꾹 눌러서 풀어 주는 것을 말해요. 일상에서는 '지압을 하다'나 '꾹꾹 누르다'라고도 해요. '어깨를 지압하다'처럼 누르는 부분 뒤에 '를'을 써요.

phrases.en: I gave my mom's shoulders an acupressure massage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 위해 해 줄 때 써요. 윗사람에게는 '드리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing it for someone else; use 'deurida' for elders.

phrases.en: I press the sore spot firmly with my fingers.
It feels refreshing when I press the soles of my feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지압의 효과를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common connected form for describing the effect of acupressure.

explain_en: It means pressing firmly on one part of the body with fingers or palms to loosen it up. In daily talk people also say '지압을 하다' or '꾹꾹 누르다'. The pressed body part takes '를', as in '어깨를 지압하다'.
